text: US stocks fell for a fourth straight session Tuesday as the AI and chip worries continued ahead of Nvidia's earnings after the bell. The S&P 500 fell 1.0% to about 7,341, the Nasdaq dropped 0.7% and the Dow lost 1.7%, based on preliminary closing data, with every S&P sector lower. Software, airlines and banks were the weakest areas, and rate-hike expectations, higher import prices and Middle East tensions added to the caution. The TSX closed at 35,315, down 1.1%, with technology the main drag. Globally, the STOXX 600 fell 0.8% and Asia was lower too, with Korea down 2.6%, Taiwan down 2.3%, Australia down 1.8% and Japan down 1.3%.
mood: Risk-off: doubts over the AI trade, rate-hike expectations and Middle East tensions weighed on stocks worldwide ahead of Nvidia's results.

veqt.t: Lower for a fourth day: S&P 500 -1.0%, Nasdaq -0.7%, Dow -1.7%, with every sector down.
Broad selloff led by tech: TSX -1.1% to 35,315.
Europe fell on Nvidia caution (STOXX 600 -0.8%, FTSE -0.8%, DAX -0.9%), Nikkei -1.3%, ASX 200 -1.8%.
Asia weak: Hang Seng -0.9%, Kospi -2.6%, Taiwan -2.3%, Shanghai -0.6%. Nifty not found, Sensex +0.4%.
